## Why one EC2 host

The four Node services, PostgreSQL, Kafka, and frontend run on one `m7i-flex.large` Amazon Linux 2023 x86_64 host (2 vCPU, 8 GiB RAM) in `us-east-2` for the selected 24-hour Free plan demonstration. Each service still owns a distinct database and role. A single host keeps a small dev environment explainable and avoids an ALB, NAT gateway, RDS, and managed Kafka baseline bill. ECS/Fargate plus RDS/MSK would improve service lifecycle and database resilience, but brings more infrastructure and a higher minimum bill. This deployment has no high availability, automated backups, or production SLO claim. Database and Kafka volumes live on the encrypted root disk: replacing/terminating the instance loses them. Snapshot/export before replacement.

# Selected 24-hour Free plan demo: GitHub validates; local temporary credentials deploy.
# This mode does not create or manage an account-wide GitHub OIDC provider.
region                   = "us-east-2"
project                  = "linked-in-node"
github_repository        = "robertovalencia/linked-in-node-and-aws"
instance_type            = "m7i-flex.large"
enable_github_deployment = false

output "deployment_account_id" { value = data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id }

output "deployment_region" { value = var.region }

resource "aws_iam_instance_profile" "host" { role = aws_iam_role.host.name }
resource "aws_instance" "dev" {

frontend:
    image: ${FRONTEND_IMAGE:?immutable frontend digest required}
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: [127.0.0.1:80:8180]
    depends_on: [identity, catalog, inquiries, notifications]
    logging: {driver: json-file, options: {max-size: 10m, max-file: '3'}}
volumes:

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
dnf install -y docker jq python3 awscli-2
systemctl enable --now docker amazon-ssm-agent
install -d -m 0700 /opt/marketplace/releases
# Compose is vendored in release bundles from the validated CLI container in CI.
# The host uses that pinned container against its Docker socket, avoiding curl|sh.

digest=$(aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name "${repo#*/}" --image-ids "imageTag=$GITHUB_SHA" --query 'images[0].imageId.imageDigest' --output text)
            if [[ ! "$digest" =~ ^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$ ]]; then
              docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --label "org.opencontainers.image.revision=$GITHUB_SHA" --push --tag "$repo:$GITHUB_SHA" "$app"
              digest=$(aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name "${repo#*/}" --image-ids "imageTag=$GITHUB_SHA" --query 'images[0].imageId.imageDigest' --output text)
            fi
            [[ "$digest" =~ ^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$ ]]
            echo "${app^^}_IMAGE=$repo@$digest" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          done
      - name: Scan the actual published images

umask 077
release_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
cd "$release_dir"
exec 9>/opt/marketplace/deploy.lock
flock -n 9 || { echo 'Another deployment is running'; exit 1; }
secret_arn=$(jq -er .secret_arn manifest.json)
region=$(jq -er .region manifest.json)
registry=$(jq -er .backend manifest.json | cut -d/ -f1)
trap 'rm -f "$release_dir/secret.json"' EXIT
aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --region "$region" --secret-id "$secret_arn" --query SecretString --output text >secret.json
python3 - <<'PY'

KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: 1
      KAFKA_LOG_DIRS: /var/lib/kafka/data
      KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS: -Xmx512m -Xms256m
      CLUSTER_ID: MDEyMzQ1Njc4OWFiY2RlZg
    volumes: [kafka-data:/var/lib/kafka/data]

healthcheck:
    test: [CMD, node, -e, "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:'+process.env.PORT+'/health/ready').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"]
    interval: 10s
    timeout: 5s
    retries: 18
    start_period: 30s
  depends_on:
    postgres: {condition: service_healthy}
logging: {driver: json-file, options: {max-size: 10m, max-file: '3'}}

At the deadline, save required test/release evidence and export any database contents worth retaining. Check the account again. Create a fresh **saved destroy plan** from `infra/aws-dev`, review its exact resource list, then apply that same plan. The dev ECR repositories use `force_delete=true` and the versioned release bucket uses `force_destroy=true` so images and release objects are removed with the dev stack. The instance root disk has `delete_on_termination=true`. The secret enters its seven-day recovery window; [AWS says a secret marked for deletion has no charge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/manage_delete-secret.html). These settings intentionally discard demo data and release images during final cleanup. They do not run until an approved destroy is executed.
lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }

resource "aws_instance" "dev" {
  depends_on             = [aws_route_table_association.dev, aws_iam_role_policy.host, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm]
  ami                    = data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami.value
  instance_type          = var.instance_type
  subnet_id              = aws_subnet.dev.id
  vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.dev.id]
  iam_instance_profile   = aws_iam_instance_profile.host.name
  metadata_options {

deploy:
        description: 'Deploy to AWS after verification (false runs verification only)'
        type: boolean
        default: false
        required: true
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: aws-dev-release
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:

exec 9>/opt/marketplace/deploy.lock
flock -n 9 || { echo 'Another deployment is running'; exit 1; }
secret_arn=$(jq -er .secret_arn manifest.json)
region=$(jq -er .region manifest.json)
registry=$(jq -er .backend manifest.json | cut -d/ -f1)
trap 'rm -f "$release_dir/secret.json"' EXIT
aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --region "$region" --secret-id "$secret_arn" --query SecretString --output text >secret.json

if [[ "$healthy" != true ]]; then
  echo 'Health verification failed; restoring previous application images.'
  if [[ -n "$previous" && -f "$previous/compose.yaml" ]]; then
    cd "$previous"
    marketplace-compose -f compose.yaml up -d --wait --wait-timeout 180
    bash ./aws-smoke.sh
  fi
  exit 1
fi
ln -sfn "$release_dir" /opt/marketplace/current
